findings.title: Delete action is hidden for prom-rule-only list items
findings.body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `canDelete && rulerRule`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only a `promRule` to `RuleActionsButtons`/`AlertRuleMenu` (no `rulerRule`), so `rulerRule` is undefined in the new list view and the Delete item never renders even when `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` reports the user has delete permission. The delete modal already receives the identifier, so requiring a ruler DTO here unnecessarily removes delete from the list view. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test expects only four menu items, so it does not catch this regression.

findings.title: Pause action is hidden for prom-rule-only list items
findings.body: The Pause menu item is guarded by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the new prom-only list path `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Pause/Pause? menu item is never rendered even though `canPause` can be true from the new Grafana prom-rule abilities. Users lose the ability to pause Grafana rules from the list. The condition should also accept the Grafana prom rule for this path.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose pause/export/delete-permanently abilities
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`). The old ruler-based implementation used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which includes recording rules, so Grafana-managed recording rules now lose these abilities and their menu entries in the prom-only list. Use a predicate covering all Grafana prom rules or explicitly handle recording rules.

findings.title: Federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`. Previously this path called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, so federated rule groups were included in `immutableRule` and edit/delete/pause/restore/delete-permanently abilities were disabled. Consumers of `useAlertRuleAbility` on federated Mimir groups will now be shown mutation actions that the backend rejects.

findings.title: skipToken still grants the Grafana duplicate ability
findings.body: When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` receives `skipToken`, they call `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, but that function still sets `MaybeSupported` to `AlwaysSupported` (when not loading) and builds abilities from `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`. In particular `Duplicate` becomes `[true, true]` for any user with Grafana `AlertingRuleCreate`. `AlertRuleMenu` calls this with `skipToken` for non-Grafana `promRule`s and ORs `canDuplicate` with the ruler ability, so a user with Grafana create permission but without external-rule write permission can see Duplicate on data source rules. `skipToken` should yield all-false abilities.

findings.title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
findings.body: In the `origin === 'grafana'` switch branch, the mapped `GrafanaRuleListItem` is returned without the computed `key`. The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` used `key={key}`. These items contain stateful action components and the list grows while paginating, so missing keys can cause React to reuse the wrong instance/state and emits duplicate-key warnings. Pass the computed key.

findings.title: Grafana rule list links no longer preserve returnTo
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the view URL with `createReturnTo()`. The new component builds `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` without a `returnTo` parameter, so navigating from a filtered list to a rule (and then to edit) no longer preserves the list/filter location as the return target. Add `returnTo` as before.

findings.title: Group loader comment still mentions Ruler loading
findings.body: The component doc comment still says it 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', but this PR removed the Ruler query and the component now only uses Prometheus. Update the comment to avoid misleading future changes.
